signal: Gearbox HS bearing running hotter than its siblings at the same load
aiInterpretation: HS-shaft bearing temperature has climbed about 14 °C against load since 06:00, with the gearbox oil debris count rising alongside it — the classic early signature of bearing surface damage.

detail.signal: WTG-05 HS bearing is 89 °C at 14:00; the other running Feeder 1 turbines, at the same power, read 75–76 °C.
detail.observed: Bearing temperature trend diverges from the power-normalised fleet trend from 06:00; oil debris counter up from ~3 to ~22 particles/h; HS bearing vibration up ~0.9 mm/s.
detail.derived: Temperature residual (actual minus load/ambient model) is rising steadily, not stepping — consistent with progressive wear rather than a sensor offset.
detail.inferred: Early-stage HS bearing damage (spalling). Weeks, not hours, to functional failure at this rate, but trending the wrong way.
detail.recommendation: Keep running with a lower temperature alarm; schedule borescope and oil sample at the next low-wind window; order a replacement bearing kit.

relatedOccurrences.summary: WTG-11 HS bearing replaced after a similar 3-week temperature and debris trend.

detail.whatChangedSummary: No maintenance or setpoint change on WTG-05 in the window — the trend is intrinsic.

whatChanged.description: Bearing temperature residual crosses the 2σ band.
Oil debris counter reading confirmed on site.

detail.confidence: Two independent signals agree (temperature and oil debris)
detail.risk: High if ignored — a failed HS bearing can take the gearbox with it

signal: Generator winding temperature climbed, fan motor had stopped
aiInterpretation: The winding temperature rise looked like a generator problem, but it started exactly when the cooling fan motor current dropped to zero — the generator was fine, its cooling had stopped.

detail.signal: WTG-03 stator winding temperature rose 64 °C between 09:20 and 11:10 at steady load.
detail.observed: Cooling fan motor current fell from ~9 A to 0 A at 09:40; the winding temperature started climbing within the next interval.
detail.derived: Load and ambient were unchanged, so the heat input didn’t change — the heat removal did.
detail.inferred: Fan motor protection tripped; the generator itself was healthy.
detail.recommendation: Reset the fan motor breaker, then watch the winding temperature come back down before closing out.
detail.whatChangedSummary: Fan motor breaker reset remotely at 11:20; winding temperature back to normal by 12:10.

whatChanged.description: Cooling fan current 0 A.
Generator thermal derate applied by the turbine controller.
Fan motor breaker reset remotely.

detail.confidence: Confirmed — temperature fell as soon as the fan restarted
detail.risk: Low — caught before a winding over-temperature trip

signal: Feeder 2 tripped and took seven turbines offline
aiInterpretation: All seven Feeder 2 turbines stopped in the same interval — a feeder-level event, not seven turbine faults. WTG-10’s pad transformer had been heating with no matching load before the trip.

detail.signal: Feeder 2 output fell from 8.4 MW to 0 at 10:10; export dropped by the same amount.
detail.observed: Feeder breaker opened on ground fault; WTG-07…13 all lost grid at the same time; WTG-10 transformer oil temperature had risen 19 °C since 09:20 at constant load.
detail.derived: The only asset with an abnormal trend before the trip was WTG-10’s pad transformer — the likely origin.
detail.inferred: Internal fault in WTG-10’s pad-mount transformer; its own protection didn’t clear it, so the feeder breaker did.
detail.recommendation: Isolate WTG-10 at its loop-feed switches, re-energise Feeder 2, and keep WTG-10 out of service for transformer testing.
detail.whatChangedSummary: WTG-10 isolated at 10:40; Feeder 2 re-energised at 10:50 without it. Six turbines back online.

whatChanged.description: Feeder 2 breaker trip, ground fault.
WTG-10 transformer isolated at loop-feed switches.
Feeder 2 breaker closed.

detail.confidence: Confirmed by field crew (oil discoloration, pressure relief operated)
detail.risk: Contained — WTG-10 out of service until the transformer is replaced
detail.expectedOutcome: Feeder 2 restored; WTG-10 transformer replacement planned

signal: Nacelle wind speed read low on WTG-12 while it kept producing normally
aiInterpretation: WTG-12 reported roughly a third less wind than its neighbours and the met mast, but its power stayed where they are — the measurement was wrong, not the wind.

detail.signal: At 08:20 WTG-12 reported 4.0 m/s while the met mast read 6.5 m/s.
detail.observed: Power output tracked the neighbours; power-curve performance computed against its own wind reading jumped above 120%.
detail.derived: Nothing else corroborated a low-wind condition — rotor speed, pitch and power all said normal wind.
detail.inferred: Iced nacelle anemometer (ambient −5 °C, humidity 97%); anemometer heater circuit had tripped.
detail.recommendation: Reset the anemometer heater and confirm the reading returns to the met-mast reference.

detail.risk: Low — control uses the reading for yaw and cut-out, but power was unaffected

signal: Converter tripped on a phase-module fault after a humid, low-load morning
aiInterpretation: Cabinet humidity rose through the cold low-wind morning; the converter tripped as load ramped back up. Field data shows most converter faults are moisture-related, not heat-related.

detail.signal: WTG-09 converter tripped at 12:30 on a phase-module fault; turbine restarted 13:10 after cabinet heaters ran.
detail.observed: Cabinet humidity climbed from 55% to 72% between 06:00 and 12:20 through a cold, low-load morning; converter temperature was normal.
detail.derived: Trip happened on the load ramp, with no over-temperature — pointing at condensation, not thermal stress.
detail.inferred: Condensation on the phase module; the cabinet heater thermostat may be set too low for this cold spell.
detail.recommendation: Keep running; check the cabinet heater thermostat and inspect the phase module for moisture tracking at the next visit.
detail.whatChangedSummary: Restarted 13:10 after heaters ran for 40 minutes; humidity falling.

whatChanged.description: Converter phase-module fault, turbine stopped.
Remote restart after cabinet heating.

detail.confidence: Likely — consistent with field studies, not yet inspected
detail.risk: Medium — a repeat trip could damage the module
detail.expectedOutcome: Humidity back below 50% within the hour

signal: WTG-14 keeps stopping on pitch battery checks — four times since 11:50
aiInterpretation: Each stop is short and the turbine restarts on its own, but the pitch backup battery is too weak to guarantee feathering the blades on a grid loss. The stops will keep coming and the safety margin is gone.

detail.signal: Pitch backup battery voltage is 206 V (nominal ~238 V); four automatic safety stops since 11:50.
detail.observed: Battery voltage has been falling since midnight; each stop takes 5–7 minutes, then the turbine auto-restarts.
detail.derived: Stops are getting closer together (50, 40, 30 minutes apart) as the battery gets weaker in the cold.
detail.inferred: End-of-life pitch battery pack; cold weather is pushing it under the test threshold.
detail.recommendation: Stop WTG-14 and keep it stopped until the battery pack is replaced — without it, the blades may not feather on a grid loss.

signal: WTG-17 producing ~5% under its power curve, with nothing reported wrong
aiInterpretation: WTG-17 is available and running, and its measured yaw error reads near zero — yet it’s steadily below its curve while its Feeder 3 neighbours aren’t. That combination points at a wind vane that’s pointing the wrong way.

detail.signal: WTG-17 has averaged 95% of its power curve since 08:00, versus 99% for the other healthy Feeder 3 turbines.
detail.observed: Availability 100%; measured yaw error averages ~0°; nacelle direction sits ~11° off the met-mast wind direction.
detail.derived: A steady ~11° misalignment explains a ~5% loss (cos² to cos³ law); the controller can’t see it because it trusts the vane.
detail.inferred: Wind vane offset after yesterday’s vane replacement.
detail.recommendation: Check the vane’s north-mark alignment against the nacelle axis and correct the offset parameter.
detail.whatChangedSummary: Wind vane replaced on WTG-17 yesterday afternoon.

whatChanged.description: Underperformance flagged after a full night of data.

detail.confidence: Medium — pattern fits, not yet checked on site
detail.risk: Low safety risk; ~5% lost energy on this turbine until fixed

signal: Feeder 4 turbines under their power curve in freezing fog — blade icing
aiInterpretation: Performance fell on all five Feeder 4 turbines together at −5 °C and 97% humidity, worst on WTG-22, and recovered as the temperature rose above freezing.

detail.signal: WTG-22 fell to 78% of its power curve at 07:30; the other Feeder 4 machines averaged 91%.
detail.observed: Ambient −5 °C and 97% humidity at the met mast; rotor speed lower than expected for the wind; no fault codes.
detail.derived: A site-wide, weather-correlated loss on one feeder (the ridge-top string) is a signature of icing, not of any one machine.
detail.inferred: Rime ice on the blades of the exposed Feeder 4 string.
detail.recommendation: Keep running while ice-throw risk is managed (access restrictions); watch recovery as it warms.

relatedOccurrences.summary: Feeder 4 icing event, 6 hours, similar pattern.

detail.whatChangedSummary: Ambient crossed 0 °C at ~10:30; performance back to normal by 11:00.

detail.confidence: High — pattern, weather and recovery all agree
